# 1 Kings Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel — all the tribal leaders and heads of families — in Jerusalem, to bring the ark of the LORD's covenant up from the City of David, that is, Zion.

**2** All the men of Israel came together before King Solomon during the festival in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month.

**3** When all the elders arrived, the priests took up the ark

**4** and brought it up, along with the tent of meeting and all its sacred furnishings. The priests and Levites carried them.

**5** King Solomon and the entire congregation of Israel gathered before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that no one could keep count.

**6** The priests brought the ark of the LORD's covenant to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple — the Most Holy Place — beneath the wings of the cherubim.

**7** The cherubim's wings spread over the place where the ark rested, sheltering the ark and its carrying poles from above.

**8** The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, though not from outside. They remain there to this day.

**9** There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites after they came out of Egypt.

**10** When the priests withdrew from the Holy Place, a cloud filled the temple of the LORD.

**11** The priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud — the glory of the LORD had filled the temple.

**12** Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said he would live in a dark cloud.

**13** I have built a magnificent temple for you — a place for you to live forever."

**14** The king turned to face the whole assembly of Israel, who were standing, and he blessed them.

**15** He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made a promise to my father David and has now fulfilled it with his own hand.

**16** He said, 'From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have never chosen a city in any tribe of Israel for a temple to be built for my name. But I chose David to rule my people Israel.'

**17** My father David set his heart on building a temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**18** But the LORD told my father David, 'It is good that you wanted to build a temple for my name.

**19** But you are not the one who will build it. Your own son — he will build the temple for my name.'

**20** The LORD has kept the promise he made. I have succeeded my father David and now sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised. I have built this temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**21** And I have provided a place there for the ark containing the covenant the LORD made with our ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt."

**22** Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD, facing the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven.

**23** He prayed: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you — in heaven above or on earth below. You keep your covenant and show faithful love to your servants who walk before you wholeheartedly.

**24** You have kept the promise you made to your servant, my father David. With your own mouth you promised it, and with your own hand you have fulfilled it today.

**25** Now, LORD God of Israel, keep the other promise you made to my father David: 'You will always have a descendant sitting on the throne of Israel — if your sons are careful to walk before me as you have walked before me.'

**26** God of Israel, please confirm the word you spoke to your servant David.

**27** But will God really live on earth? The heavens — even the highest heavens — cannot contain you. How much less this temple I have built!

**28** Yet, LORD my God, hear the prayer and the plea your servant is making before you today.

**29** May your eyes be open toward this temple day and night — this place of which you said, 'My name will be there' — so that you will hear the prayer your servant prays facing this place.

**30** Hear the plea of your servant and your people Israel when they pray facing this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.

**31** When someone wrongs another person and is required to take an oath, and they come and swear before your altar in this temple —

**32** hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: condemn the guilty and bring their actions down on their own heads, and vindicate the innocent by treating them as their innocence deserves.

**33** When your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and when they turn back to you, acknowledge your name, and pray and plead before you in this temple —

**34** hear from heaven, forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.

**35** When the skies are shut and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and when they pray facing this place, acknowledge your name, and turn from their sin because you have humbled them —

**36** hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave your people as their inheritance.

**37** When famine or plague strikes the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or caterpillars — or when an enemy besieges any of their cities — whatever disaster or disease comes —

**38** when any prayer or plea is made by anyone among your people Israel, each one aware of their own suffering and spreading their hands toward this temple —

**39** hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive and respond. Deal with each person according to all their ways, since you know their heart — for you alone know every human heart —

**40** so that they may reverence you all the days they live in the land you gave our ancestors.

**41** And when a foreigner — someone who is not one of your people Israel — comes from a distant land because of your reputation,

**42** because they have heard about your great name, your mighty power, and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray facing this temple,

**43** hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you. Do this so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and reverence you, just as your people Israel do, and so they may know that this temple I have built bears your name.

**44** When your people go to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD facing the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name —

**45** hear their prayer and their plea from heaven and uphold their cause.

**46** When they sin against you — and there is no one who does not sin — and you become angry with them and hand them over to their enemies, who carry them away as captives to their own land, whether far or near,

**47** and when they come to their senses in the land of their exile and repent and plead with you, saying, 'We have sinned; we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly' —

**48** and when they turn back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and pray to you facing the land you gave their ancestors, the city you chose, and the temple I built for your name —

**49** then hear their prayer and their plea from heaven, your dwelling place, and uphold their cause.

**50** Forgive your people who have sinned against you. Forgive all their offenses against you. Cause their captors to show them mercy,

**51** for they are your people, your inheritance — the ones you brought out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace.

**52** May your eyes be open to your servant's plea and to the plea of your people Israel, listening to them whenever they cry out to you.

**53** For you set them apart from all the peoples of the earth to be your inheritance, just as you declared through your servant Moses when you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, O Lord GOD."

**54** When Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and plea to the LORD, he rose from before the altar where he had been kneeling with his hands spread toward heaven.

**55** He stood and blessed the entire assembly of Israel in a loud voice:

**56** "Praise the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not a single word has failed of all the good promises he made through his servant Moses.

**57** May the LORD our God be with us as he was with our ancestors. May he never leave us or abandon us.

**58** May he turn our hearts toward him, so that we walk in all his ways and keep the commands, laws, and rules he gave our ancestors.

**59** And may these words of mine — this prayer I have offered before the LORD — be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that he may uphold the cause of his servant and of his people Israel, according to each day's need.

**60** Then all the peoples of the earth will know that the LORD is God. There is no other.

**61** And may your hearts be fully committed to the LORD our God, living by his decrees and keeping his commands, as you are doing today."

**62** Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.

**63** Solomon's fellowship offerings to the LORD totaled twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. In this way the king and all Israel dedicated the temple of the LORD.

**64** That same day the king consecrated the central part of the courtyard in front of the temple, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings. So he offered them there in the courtyard.

**65** Solomon and all Israel celebrated the festival at that time — a huge assembly of people from as far away as Lebo-hamath in the north to the Brook of Egypt in the south. They celebrated before the LORD our God for seven days, and then seven more days — fourteen days in all.

**66** On the following day he sent the people home. They blessed the king and went to their homes with joyful and grateful hearts for all the good things the LORD had done for his servant David and for his people Israel.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **8:10-11 — the glory descends**: The moment the ark reaches its resting place, God shows up so powerfully that the priests can't function. This is the exact same phenomenon that happened when the tabernacle was completed (Exodus 40). The message: the God of the wilderness is now the God of the temple. The presence is the same.

2. **8:27 — "the highest heavens cannot contain you"**: The most theologically sophisticated sentence Solomon ever speaks. He has just built the most magnificent building in the ancient world — and immediately acknowledges that it cannot hold God. The temple is real presence without containment. This is the biblical paradox of sacred space.

3. **8:41-43 — prayer for foreigners**: In the middle of dedicating Israel's national temple, Solomon prays for outsiders — people from other nations who will come seeking God. This is not an afterthought. It is the temple's purpose: to be a beacon for the nations, not a wall against them.

4. **8:46 — "there is no one who does not sin"**: Solomon states what the whole Bible assumes: universal human failure. This is not pessimism but realism, and it is the foundation for the entire prayer's logic — if everyone sins, everyone needs a mechanism for forgiveness.

5. **8:46-50 — praying from exile**: Solomon prays for a future that will not arrive for four centuries: the exile. He envisions Israelites in a foreign land, turning toward Jerusalem, and praying. This prayer will sustain Jewish worship through the Babylonian exile, through the destruction of the second temple, and through every diaspora since. Daniel 6:10 is the living fulfillment of this text.

— PNEUMA
